report.source_text: Given the worsening symptomatology due to the septic scenario sustained by empyema in the right pleural cavity, the patient was referred to a tertiary thoracic surgery department for management. A right thoracotomy surgery, with video-thoracoscopic assistance, was performed to remove the cyst, reduce the infectious burden, and perform a pleural debridement. Despite clinical improvement, a redo-surgery was necessary to repair a bronchopleural fistulation one week later. After completely recovering the right pleuropulmonary side, the hydatid cyst on the left lung, which also ruptured into bronchioles, was treated surgically using a total minimally invasive technique (Figure 2). The patient was discharged on postoperative day 23 after the first operation.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old woman presented with severe chest pain, dyspnea, coughing, vomiting, fever, progressive weight loss, intermittent fever, and abdominal distension, with a history of farm animal exposure. Chest CT revealed bilateral voluminous lung cysts, one ruptured with empyema and the other showing a water-lily sign. Abdominal ultrasound and CT identified a giant hepatic cyst (16 cm, CE3a). Serological tests (ELISA and Western Blot) confirmed antibodies against Echinococcus spp. The patient underwent right thoracotomy for the ruptured lung cyst, followed by a redo-surgery for bronchopleural fistulation, and later surgery for the left lung cyst. Molecular analysis of surgical material confirmed E. granulosus sensu stricto (s.s.), G1 genotype. The hepatic cyst was treated with PAIR ultrasound-guided needle alcoholization. The patient showed complete recovery without signs of local recurrence at one month post-treatment.
